newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hannover Re sees strong 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: Hannover Re sees strong 1996 profits.

text.p: Hannover Re, the world's fifth largest reinsurance group, on Friday said it expected a double digit rise in its 1996 pre-tax profits on the back of an advance of more than 20 percent in investment earnings.

In an interim report, the German insurer, whose full name is Hannover Rueckversicherungs AG, said it had increased its capital investment portfolio over the year to 13.8 billion marks ($8.4 billion) on an unconsolidated basis.

That would lead to investment returns of some 750 million marks so that despite weaker underwriting earnings, pre-tax profits would rise to 130 million marks from 116 million -- a move the company said would be passed on to investors.
Hannover Re paid a dividend of three marks per share on 1995 profits, which also showed an overall advance despite a group underwriting loss of 20.3 million marks.
In general, the insurer said, business had been "very pleasing" at both parent and group level, and gross premium income increased by three percent to around 6.2 billion marks.
However underwriting returns were likely to fall further because of expansion costs, particularly in the life and health insurance segments.

Hannover Re, which has units in 13 countries and is active in 100 countries worldwide, is targeting expansion in the U.S., Japan and South East Asia as well as an increased market share in life insurance.
Its stock, which is shortly to join Germany's MDAX mid-cap index, was up two marks on Friday at 81.50 marks.
Hannover Re said the German bourse's decision to include its stock in the 70-share MDAX had been very helpful for its share price.
Elevation to the MDAX, which with the blue chip DAX forms Germany's 100 top stocks, is generally expected to boost liquidity in a stock and enhance the company's profile in general.
